title: Logbook disclosure to law enforcement, the limits on other use, and the prohibited acts that reach a regulated seller's employees and agents
subtopic: Logbook disclosure and the prohibited acts of sellers, employees and agents
rule_summary: Under 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(C), in order to protect the privacy of individuals who purchase scheduled listed chemical products, the Attorney General shall by regulation establish restrictions on disclosure of information in logbooks under 830(e)(1)(A)(iii), and the regulations shall provide for the disclosure of the information as appropriate to the Attorney General and to State and local law enforcement agencies and prohibit accessing, using, or sharing information in the logbooks for any purpose other than to ensure compliance with the subchapter or to facilitate a product recall to protect public health and safety. 21 CFR 1314.45 restricts the disclosure of information in logbooks under 21 CFR 1314.30 as follows: (a) the information shall be disclosed as appropriate to the Administration and to State and local law enforcement agencies; (b) the information in the logbooks shall not be accessed, used, or shared for any purpose other than to ensure compliance with this title or to facilitate a product recall to protect public health and safety; and (c) a regulated seller who in good faith releases information in a logbook to Federal, State, or local law enforcement authorities is immune from civil liability for the release unless the release constitutes gross negligence or intentional, wanton, or willful misconduct. 21 U.S.C. 830(e)(1)(E) states the same immunity for a regulated seller who in good faith releases information in a logbook under 830(e)(1)(A)(iii). Under 21 U.S.C. 842(a)(14) it is unlawful for any person who is a regulated seller or an employee or agent of such seller to disclose, in violation of regulations under 830(e)(1)(C), information in logbooks under 830(e)(1)(A)(iii), or to refuse to provide such a logbook to Federal, State, or local law enforcement authorities. Under 842(c)(1)(A), except as provided in 842(c)(1)(B), (C) or (D) and 842(c)(2), any person who violates section 842 is subject to a civil penalty; subparagraphs (B) through (D) address violations of 842(a)(5), (10), (16) and (17). Under 842(c)(2)(A), if a violation of section 842 is prosecuted by an information or indictment which alleges that the violation was committed knowingly and the trier of fact specifically finds that it was so committed, the person shall, except as otherwise provided in 842(c)(2)(B) or (D), be sentenced to imprisonment of not more than one year or a fine under title 18, or both, and under 842(c)(3), except under the conditions specified in 842(c)(2), a violation of section 842 does not constitute a crime. 21 CFR 1300.02 defines a regulated seller as a retail distributor (including a pharmacy or a mobile retail vendor), except that the term does not include an employee or agent of the distributor.
exam_relevance: Tests that logbook information shall be disclosed as appropriate to DEA and to State and local law enforcement agencies, that access, use and sharing are otherwise limited to compliance and product recalls, that a seller's good-faith release to law enforcement carries civil immunity, and that 21 U.S.C. 842(a)(14) makes unlawful disclosure of logbook information, or refusal to provide the logbook to Federal, State or local law enforcement, a prohibited act for a regulated seller's employees and agents as well as for the seller.

authority.name: Regulation of listed chemicals and certain machines

numeric_facts.fact: Maximum imprisonment for a violation of 21 U.S.C. 842 found to have been committed knowingly
numeric_facts.conditions: 21 U.S.C. 842(c)(2)(A): prosecuted by an information or indictment alleging a knowing violation, with a specific finding by the trier of fact; imprisonment, a fine under title 18, or both, except as otherwise provided in 842(c)(2)(B) or (D)

exceptions: A regulated seller who in good faith releases information in a logbook to Federal, State, or local law enforcement authorities is immune from civil liability for the release unless the release constitutes gross negligence or intentional, wanton, or willful misconduct.
common_confusions: 21 CFR 1314.45(a) provides that logbook information shall be disclosed as appropriate to the Administration and to State and local law enforcement agencies; disclosure to them is not framed as merely permitted.

The definition of regulated seller in 21 CFR 1300.02 excludes an employee or agent of the retail distributor, but 21 U.S.C. 842(a)(14) names the seller's employees and agents: disclosing logbook information in violation of the privacy regulations, or refusing to provide the logbook to Federal, State, or local law enforcement authorities, is unlawful for them as well as for the seller.
The restriction in 21 CFR 1314.45(b) is stated for the information in the logbooks, not for the seller alone.
A violation of 21 U.S.C. 842 is a crime only if it is prosecuted as, and specifically found to have been, committed knowingly; otherwise it carries a civil penalty.
